newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks end at another yearly high of 746.36.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks end at another yearly high of 746.36.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed at another yearly high on Friday as investors continued to believed in a coming economic turnaround and falling interest rates, brokers said.
They said better-than-expected macroeconomic indicators also boosted investor hopes for an economic recovery.
The composite stock index added 3.86 points, or 0.52 percent, to 746.36, off an intraday high of 752.29.
Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds fell to 11.85 percent on Friday, down from 11.86 percent on Thrusday.

"When the economy hits rock bottom and is just about to turn around, a bull is usually seen in the stock market. This is that very time," said Ahn Hyo-moon, a fundmanager at Korea Investment Trust Co.

Brokers said investors generally shrugged off President Kim Young-sam's apology on Friday over 1992 election spending abuses as his speech had nothing substantial. Even though opposition parties declared all-out war against Kim to reveal the truth, investors questioned its implementation, they said.

Industrial output in April rose 10.7 percent year-on-year, up from an 8.4 percent rise a year earlier. Inflation, gauged by the consumer price index, rose 3.8 percent in May on the year, the lowest monthly increase in 10 years.

But Korean businesses expect the economy to remain in a slump in June compared to a year ago, even though their outlook has improved from May. The Business Survey Index (BSI), provided by Federation of Korean Industries, stood at 84 for June, against 86 for the same month a year earlier and 75 for May.
A BSI of less than 100 indicates a bearish outlook.
Brokers said the indicators fuelled investor optimism about the economy and the future market direction.

Cha Hee-gun of Sunkyong Securities said investors' sentiment was bolstered by news that cabinet members were working on economic and political reforms after President's speech. A government official said ministers met but gave no details.
"I'm sure the market is riding a bull-run," said Chung Dong-bae of Daewoo Securities. "The index will rise to the 800 level in June. After a consolidation, it will head for the 900 mark this year."
Foreigners' interest also remained strong in the idea Korea would benefit most in Asia from the yen's strength, he said.

Interest-sensitive construction and financial shares continued to be in strong demand. Sub-indices for construction and securities gained 7.76 points to 297.64 and 3.86 points to 1,211.23 respectively.

Inchon Iron and Steel Co recorded a 1997 high of 19,800 won and Hyundai Pipe went limit up to 8,420 won on market rumours the Hyundai Group HYGR.CN would soon be approved to build an integrated steel mill. But a Hyundai spokesman said he had not heard such news yet.-- Yeom Yoon-jeong (822) 727 5647
